Professor Byrne is definitely one of the best, genuine, and respectful English teachers in the university. It is very clear that he is an expert in the subject and that he has genuine interest and love for what he does. He is really understanding and tries his best to better our skills. He is not hesitant to give time for his students when they need so. He is also very responsive to questions both through emails and messages, hence, the student feels comfortable in contacting him. I don't think he really has any weak points. It was a great experience to have him for ENG102!

Mr. Byrne definitely cares about the education of his students. He makes this clear at many points throughout the course. And I've definitely felt a mix of proud and lucky to be able to take this course from someone whom I knew cared about how well I was learning things. The way he talks and his general demeanor is nice and comforting to listen to, I think. He also gives extensive feedback to graded tasks, which is something you come to expect from him. However, in terms of communication, there were some aspects I found to be lacking at times. I certainly appreciate the feedback, but the feedback concerned a point that has been ingrained so deep in my writing style that I felt much uncertainty as to how I could go about improving it. I think the short coming here was that he expected the student to find a way mostly on his own, but I would've liked a more hand-holding approach in this case. I would've liked the approach to be "Try fix it, but if you can't we will fix it together" rather than "Try fixing it, but if you can't, you'll have to see your grade lowered as a direct result". To be honest, I understand that such attention would be hard to give to all students across two sections, but it is simply something I couldn't help but feel. Also considering the fact that the topic he has chosen (consciousness) is not an easy one to delve into, although I like that he does this to push you out of your comfort zone, his style is similar to tossing you in the ocean so you have to learn to swim, or you drown. All in all, I'm still happy that I was able to spend the semester with him, and I would recommend him to anyone seeking a nice challenge. He is definitely a good person whom you should experience for yourself!

instructor:
We never dwelled on topics such as how to write an essay or research paper. We studied all the lessons on consciousness, which is only the course topic. I don't think this is what should be done. We also had to learn technical information. When we asked how the research paper was written, he said "basically longer essay". But I later learned that this was not true.

I know that 6 hours a week is not required for the technical knowledge to be learned in the English course and we have this time to give the student more thinking and research skills, but I do not think that I have gained these in this course. I had to do a lot of research myself just to learn how to write essays and research papers.

In the oral presentation we made, I got  21/22 . And the reason why 1 point was broken was because I looked at my notes so much that I think I deserve this grade. But when we sent an outline of the presentation we made, he deducted points from me because my topic was not arguable, so ı had to start all over again to a research paper that took a long time to write, and I had to find a new topic in a short time. However, right after my presentation, I went to him and asked him what I was doing right and wrong, and he didn't tell me anything about it. When I mentioned this later, he used the expression "I was very soft". I need a teacher who criticizes on the spot, not a high grade teacher. I am aware that Byrne is a talented teacher, but he needs to reflect this on his students in his class. While everyone got ideas from other students for the research paper, I couldn't get the opinions of other students because I had to find a new topic and I had a harder time finding my arguments. This situation should not have happened. While I hadn't even prepared the presentation yet, Byrne was supposed to tell me after seeing my position that the position was not arguable and that I had to change it.
